sections.name: File setup, AttrType, AttributeSpec, IndustryRole, GateOverride, IndustryConfig
sections.title: Shapes for industry settings
sections.what: Defines the allowed field types, the shape of one field to collect, the shape of one role, the optional change to a maturity gate, and the full set of settings for one industry. Each industry setting holds a capacity label and unit, its fields, its roles, optional gate changes, and a flag for a segment chooser.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Having one shape for every industry's settings means all of them are read the same way.
sections.watch_out: The segment chooser flag and the gate overrides are optional, so code that reads them must handle the case where they are missing.

sections.name: DEFAULT_ROLES
sections.title: Standard roles every industry shares
sections.what: Lists eleven default roles, such as owner, operator, EPC contractor and regulator, each with a short definition. These are the parties a project can have, and industries without their own role list use this one.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the definitions themselves.
sections.watch_out: The role keys are identifiers, and the code here does not show what stores them, so check before renaming any key.

sections.name: GENERIC_SOURCE_ATTRS, DEFAULT_CONFIG
sections.title: Shared free-text fields and fallback settings
sections.what: Defines a set of plain text fields kept from source spreadsheets, such as region, description, schedule notes and cost notes. It also defines fallback settings with no unit and no custom fields, used for any industry without its own entry.
sections.why: The comment states the purpose: the free-text fields keep the original source columns so nothing is lost at import, even when a number cannot be read.
sections.watch_out: The fallback has an empty unit, so projects from an industry without its own settings will have no unit.

sections.name: INDUSTRY_CONFIGS, getIndustryConfig, getIndustryRoles, getIndustryAttributes, getCapacityUnit (part 1)
sections.title: Settings for nuclear, dairy and renewables start
sections.what: Starts the per-industry settings with nuclear, dairy and the first part of renewables. Each entry sets the capacity label and unit, the custom fields, the roles, and sometimes replacement wording for gate labels.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the setting names. The gate wording appears to replace the standard gate labels for these two industries.
sections.watch_out: Nothing here checks that an entry's key matches its slug, so a mismatch would silently apply the wrong settings.

sections.name: INDUSTRY_CONFIGS, getIndustryConfig, getIndustryRoles, getIndustryAttributes, getCapacityUnit (part 2)
sections.title: Renewables, batteries, data centers and oil and gas
sections.what: Finishes the renewables settings with its report and wind fields and extra roles, then adds settings for batteries, data centers and oil and gas. The oil and gas unit is left blank on purpose so that no unit is invented.
sections.why: The code comment explains that the oil and gas dataset mixes units, so a default unit would be wrong for many projects.
sections.watch_out: Oil and gas capacity has no unit, so the app must show the reported label instead of a unit.

sections.name: INDUSTRY_CONFIGS, getIndustryConfig, getIndustryRoles, getIndustryAttributes, getCapacityUnit (part 3)
sections.title: Settings for hydrogen, mining, lithium and gas power
sections.what: Covers hydrogen, water and ports, then the mining, lithium and gas power settings, which repeat a long list of project fields. Each sets its own capacity label and unit.
sections.why: Likely reason: the field lists are copied per industry so that each can differ. The code does not state this.
sections.watch_out: The mining and lithium field lists are almost identical, so an edit to one often needs the same change in the other.

sections.name: INDUSTRY_CONFIGS, getIndustryConfig, getIndustryRoles, getIndustryAttributes, getCapacityUnit (part 4)
sections.title: Gas power end and lookup helpers
sections.what: Finishes the gas power settings and the aerospace, ports and real estate settings, closes the list, and adds four lookup helpers. The helpers return an industry's full settings, roles, fields or unit, and use the fallback for unknown slugs.
sections.why: Likely reason: the helpers let other parts of the app ask for one piece of settings without reading the whole list.
sections.watch_out: An unknown slug gets the fallback settings with no warning, so a mistyped slug looks like a normal industry.

summary: This file declares the shapes of the per-industry settings, such as the capacity unit, the fields to collect, and the roles people play in a project.
purpose: It defines the vocabulary that each industry's configuration must follow, so other code can read those settings the same way for every industry.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Shared type definitions let the compiler catch mistakes in industry settings.
how: The file imports the maturity gate keys and then declares the allowed field types, the shape of one field, the shape of one role, the optional per-gate overrides, and the full shape of one industry's configuration. The remaining sections that build the actual configurations are not shown here.
inputs: Not visible in the section shown. The configuration data itself is listed in later sections that were not provided.
outputs: Type definitions only, with no runtime output in the section shown.
risks: Changing a type can break every industry configuration that uses it. The override field lets an industry rename or hide a maturity gate, so an override with a wrong gate key may be ignored or cause errors.
debug: If a configuration fails to load, check that its fields match these shapes, especially the field type names and the gate keys imported from the maturity file.
